title: Late Fees and Termination for Non-Payment on Resort Club Memberships Accounts
content:
An invoice on a Resort Club Memberships account that is not paid within the level's grace period, in calendar days of its entry date, is late, and a late fee of the level's late fee amount is charged on it once.

## Rules

1. **When an invoice is late.** A late fee is charged only once the grace period of the invoice has passed. The grace period ends at the close of the calendar day that falls the level's number of grace days after the invoice's entry date; a payment on that day is on time.
2. **One late fee per invoice.** Each invoice carries at most one late fee.
3. **Termination for non-payment.** When the oldest unpaid invoice of the membership has stayed unpaid for the level's non-payment threshold in calendar days, the membership is terminated for non-payment and the amounts owed remain due. An active membership passes directly to terminated in this way.
4. **Members under notice.** A member whose signed cancellation notice has been received is terminated at the end of the notice period instead, under the cancellation terms of Resort Club Memberships.

## The oldest unpaid invoice

The oldest unpaid invoice is the invoice with the earliest entry date, over the whole life of the membership up to the day of handling, that is not fully covered by the payments and credits naming it. Every kind of invoice on the club account counts:

- the initiation fee;
- dues invoices;
- freeze fees;
- food and beverage minimum charges;
- member charges signed at resort outlets;
- guest fees;
- late fees;
- early termination charges.

An invoice partly paid or partly credited is still unpaid for this purpose until payments and credits naming it cover it in full.

## Counting the grace period (hypothetical dates)

At a level whose grace period is 10 days, for an invoice entered on 1 March:

| Day | Position of the invoice |
|---|---|
| 1 March | Entry date of the invoice |
| 11 March | Last day of the grace period; the grace period ends at the close of this day, and a payment made on this day is on time |
| 12 March | The grace period has passed; if the invoice is still unpaid it is late and the late fee may be charged |

A late fee entered on 11 March would be charged before the grace period had passed, and is not charged on that day.

## Points of judgement

- **A late invoice already carrying a late fee:** no second late fee is charged on it.
- **A late fee itself unpaid:** the late fee is an invoice on the account and counts in finding the oldest unpaid invoice.
- **Termination for non-payment and the balance:** terminating the membership does not clear what is owed; the amounts owed remain due.
